articles.title: Kariobangi North Residents Raise Concern Over Rising Insecurity
articles.content:
Residents of Kariobangi North have raised concern over a recent rise in insecurity, citing an increase in muggings and theft cases across the estate. Many say they no longer feel safe, especially during the early morning and late evening hours.
The growing security concerns have also affected local businesses, with some traders reporting fewer customers as people avoid staying out late.
Residents are now calling on security agencies to intensify police patrols and enhance community policing to curb crime. They also urge members of the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activities to the relevant authorities.
The community hopes that swift action will help restore safety and confidence within the neighborhood.

Nairobi Gazettes New Development Control Policy to Curb Chaotic Construction
articles.desc: Nairobi gazettes a new development policy setting clear rules on zoning, height, and density — aiming to end years of unplanned construction across the city.
articles.content:
After years of construction proceeding with little consistent oversight, Nairobi now has a formal rulebook. The county has gazetted its Development Control Policy 2026, giving developers a single legal framework to follow instead of the patchwork of planning decisions that shaped the city until now.
The policy sets boundaries in four areas that have long strained the city: how tall buildings can rise, how densely a plot can be developed, which zones permit which uses, and what environmental protections a project must satisfy before approval. Officials frame this as a direct response to years of overcrowding and infrastructure pressure that resulted from developments approved without a shared standard.
Sakaja's office has positioned the policy as one piece of a wider rebuild already underway across roads, sewer capacity, and drainage — and is now calling on developers and residents to understand the new requirements before starting new projects.
